chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari from Ibn al-Qaddah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no oath for a child alongside his parent, nor for a wife alongside her husband, nor for a slave alongside his master.
ai.seo_question: Does a wife or child need to take their own oath if their husband or parent has already sworn?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'subsumption' in Islamic jurisprudence, where the oath of the head of the household or master legally covers the dependents, eliminating redundancy in legal proceedings. It reflects the hierarchical social structure of the time, emphasizing that the authority of the father, husband, or master extends to their respective dependents in matters of oath-taking. This ruling is particularly significant in contexts of debt, testimony, or contractual obligations where a single sworn statement suffices for the entire dependent unit.
